summary: Microsoft can compound durable cloud and AI growth as Azure demand converts into revenue, provided capacity additions arrive on schedule and infrastructure intensity does not structurally erode cloud economics.
authorshipLabel: Delphi Demo Team — hypothetical pre-earnings view derived from public sources

pillars.title: Azure demand remains durable
pillars.statement: Azure and AI demand should sustain mid-30s constant-currency growth as capacity comes online.

pillars.title: Capacity converts backlog into revenue
pillars.statement: Planned datacenter additions should convert strong demand into recognized Azure revenue without a prolonged constraint.

pillars.title: AI investment preserves attractive economics
pillars.statement: Efficiency gains should offset enough infrastructure cost to keep Microsoft Cloud gross margin near the high-60s while AI scale expands.

catalysts.title: Incremental AI capacity comes online
catalysts.expectedImpact: Converts constrained demand into Azure revenue

risks.title: AI capacity remains constrained
risks.description: Demand may continue to exceed available datacenter capacity and delay revenue conversion.

risks.title: AI capital intensity pressures returns
risks.description: Accelerating infrastructure spend may outpace near-term monetization and reduce cloud margin resilience.

risks.title: Large AI customer concentration
risks.description: A small number of AI labs may be both major customers and emerging platform competitors.

openQuestions.question: How long will AI capacity constraints delay Azure demand conversion?
What evidence will show that incremental AI capex is earning an attractive return?
